newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto base metal stocks up on high expectations.
newsitem.headline: Toronto base metal stocks up on high expectations.

text.p: Base metal stocks were popular on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday morning as investors anticipated higher commodity prices, analysts said.
Nickel giant Inco Ltd topped Toronto's most actives list, rising C$1.15 to C$45.25 with more than 690,000 shares trading hands by mid-morning.
Alcan Aluminum Ltd was ahead C$0.70 at C$48.65 with more than 370,000 shares traded. The Montreal-based company touched a 52-week high in early trading Monday when the stock reached C$48.70.
Toronto's base metals index was up 1.31 percent.
Investors were returning to the market after the holiday season and sinking money into base metals, mining analyst Tony Hayes at Credifinance in Toronto said.

"There's a growing movement in the U.S. over the past four or five trading days that is positive on the metal stocks," Hayes said. "News articles are coming out saying that things aren't as bad as anticipated."
Nickel and aluminum inventories on the London Metal Exchange were falling, creating a tight market, he said.
"This is likely to develop over the next three to six months," he added.
Nickel was up on the LME to a month high of US$6,945 a tonne, while aluminum traded narrowly on Monday above US$1,550 a tonne.
